title: Banda Singh’s Entry into Sirhind and the Opening of Ram Rayyas and Bhujangis

blocks.text: This transition page reflects on what happened after victory at Sirhind and how Banda handled the conquered city. The text stresses that he did not ransack the city of Sirhind completely, choosing instead a more selective policy of punishment, control, and redistribution.

That restraint is followed by local rearrangements around nearby villages and by the emergence of a new complaint involving Ram Rayyas and Bhujangis. The page therefore turns from conquest to contested governance, showing that holding territory generated new religious and political disputes.
As with many boundary pages in this book, the narrative does not stop cleanly at one event. It closes the Sirhind entry and opens the next controversy in the same breath.
